subfield: Theoretical physics: quantum gravity and string theory
motivation: Hawking's discovery that black holes radiate raised a basic question: can quantum mechanics and gravity be consistent? Susskind proposed the holographic principle, which says that the degrees of freedom of a gravitating region live on its boundary. Maldacena turned this into a precise, calculable duality between gravity in anti-de Sitter space and an ordinary quantum field theory. Witten set up the holographic dictionary, which relates bulk fields to boundary operators and a black hole to a thermal state. Together this work established that black hole evaporation is unitary, and it led to the quantum-extremal-surface derivation of the Page curve. It has become a working tool across physics, used for quark-gluon plasma transport, strongly correlated electrons, quantum chaos and quantum information. It changed how physicists think about spacetime itself, which is now understood as emerging from quantum entanglement. Few theoretical ideas of the past thirty years have reshaped a foundational question so deeply.
